clause_that_reaches_it: RESEARCH is recoverable but not versioned.
why_in_scope: Unchanged in scope from the VIOLATES filing — the tier states what research is OWED. WHY_IT_VIOLATED: a Rewrite replaced the note's whole body through an atomic DocumentStore.performFileSave with no backup, and research notes have no op log, are not walked by CheckpointCapture (allDocIds comes from manifest.structure) and left no trash copy — so an afternoon the writer spent developing that note had no route back inside Maugham, while the same content DELETED would have been recoverable (RULING-15's trash). As of the fix PromotionPerformer.preservePriorVersion keeps the note's current contents under a new TrashSubject.priorVersion, visible in the Trash pane (unlike .internalArtifact, which RULING-43 hides because nothing would point at it again). Recoverable, not versioned — exactly the tier, and no more. It is the MINIMAL bridge inside existing machinery and is expected to be superseded by GAP-P1 / research protection when research versioning is scoped. AMENDED 2026-08-09b, whole-branch review: the first fix bought the recoverability and left three holes in it, all in this ruling's own scope. (a) The keep was a MOVE, so between it and the fallible body write the note existed only in the trash — a rewrite that failed told the writer nothing had happened while their note had left the research pane, which is worse than the defect for the window it lasts. trashPriorVersion now copies the entry's file straight back to the original path before returning: the move is kept because it is what carries the typed mover's flush discipline (tripwire 14), and the net effect is a copy, so the live file never stops existing. The .update arm also re-stamps manifest.modified/saveManifest, which the arm lost when M6-PR-038 took its updateResearchItem call away. (b) The restore was invisible: .priorVersion routed to .fileOnly, correct that nothing needed rewiring and wrong that nothing needed showing — .captureAsset's file goes back where the Inbox pane is already looking, a prior version landed in research/ where nothing looks, so the writer asked for their prose back, was told it came, and no surface would ever show it to them again. It now mints a research row, '<title> (previous version)', at the path the file actually landed at (RULING-41's row-and-disk agreement). (c) The PALETTE-CARD rewrite arm had no protection at all — the same total replacement of the writer's prose, on the artifact more likely to have been developed by hand, since a card is edited in the pane rather than generated. ProjectStore.trashPriorVersionText covers it, writing the card's prior BODY into the entry rather than moving the card file, because a card's prose shares its file with the swatches, sensory notes and image references that the rewrite deliberately keeps.
intent_expressed_when: contemporaneous — the writer chose the Rewrite mode; but they were never told how much was in the note, and the preview shows only what will be written

Handing the file over instead would make promotion the one verb here that MOVES, and there is no reverse-promote to undo it with.
